title: Destination Blood Bowl ruleset
body: The Roster Builder now offers the Destination Blood Bowl ruleset (Charleston, April 2027): five tiers with 5 to 9 Skill Points, two-skill stacks for Tiers 3 to 5 at 3 Skill Points, and Star Players that cost Skill Points as well as gold, with one Mega-Star for Tier 5 teams. Squad rules (shared treasury, Squad Points, one race per squad) are checked by the organiser.

title: One team summary everywhere, now with portraits
body: The Roster Builder's Summary step now looks exactly like a league team page: the crest, the team strip and the table-style roster, with a portrait for every player, and the save line, Validator and Inducements beside it. Edit team turns on hiring and editing there, as on the league page. League team pages get the portraits too, and shared team links open the same table-style summary.

title: Team sheets always fit on one page
body: The Tournament Ruleset box at the top right of the team sheet is now wider and more compact, so long package names and skill rules sit on one line and push nothing down. The exported PDF always fits on one page: a long roster prints a little denser instead of spilling onto a second page.

title: A new admin console
body: Site admins have a new admin console in the site's own look, with Users, Teams, Games, Reports, board Moderation across leagues and tournaments, Organisers, Privacy jobs and Operations in one place. Operations covers the game server reload, the league fork cleanup, the ratings reset (it always takes a backup first, and a backup can be restored), demo leagues and the testing suite, each with a dry run first and every use logged. The old admin page now opens the new console.

title: Today's new screens match the site's look
body: Board threads now look like league news cards, Ratings numbers line up on the right like Standings, and a few spacing, colour and button-row fixes on the check-in pages, Money settings, Badges and the redraft board bring today's new screens in line with the rest of the site.

title: Bug reports can carry a reply to the player
body: Organisers can now write a reply to the player and the version a fix ships in, from the admin Reports panel or the Discord triage card. These sit apart from the private root cause and notes, and the player's own client can check the status of the reports they sent.

title: Check-in QR codes use the site's public address
body: Personal and venue check-in QR codes, and the link shown under them, now always point at the site's public address, so phones can open them even when an organiser opened the page on the host computer. If the host has no public address set, the code uses the page's own address, and organisers on this computer see a note saying phones can't open it.

title: League money defaults to the BB2025 rulebook
body: Leagues that never set their money rules now pay the BB2025 rulebook winnings: (half the fan attendance + touchdowns + 1 without stalling) x 10k, with the rulebook concession rule. Leagues that saved their own money rules keep them, games already played keep their numbers, and the old 10k per touchdown is a one-click Legacy preset. Also: the fixture summary's comparison no longer scrolls sideways on phones, and tournament organisers see an Override mark on check-ins made outside the check-in window.

title: QR check-in, and tournament times in your own time zone
body: Every coach in a tournament's field gets a personal check-in QR code on their entry: an organiser scans it at the venue, or the coach opens it while check-in is open, and it works once. Organisers can also put up a venue QR (full screen, with New code and Switch off) that coaches scan to check themselves in. Tournament times (start, registration, check-in, the registration gate) are now shown and typed in your device's time zone, and Discord posts show them in each reader's own zone.

title: Badges and achievements
body: Coaches now earn badges (first win, 10 / 50 / 100 games, unbeaten season, belt holder, tournament and Rumble winner, a 5-win streak, one per race) and achievements from recorded games and from time in leagues; they show on your coach page, the coach popup and team pages. League organisers can create their own badges and award them by hand on the league's Awards tab.

title: Coach ratings: Glicko-2 overall and per race
body: Every coach now has a Glicko-2 rating, overall and for each race they play, from league, ladder, tournament and Super FUMBBL games; forfeits and organiser overrides never count. A new Ratings page ranks coaches overall or by race, with a minimum-games filter and a Show provisional switch (a rating is provisional until 5 games). Coach cards, the fixture summary and the coach popup show the new rating, and ladders ranked by rating use it.

title: Search the whole site
body: A search bar at the top right finds leagues, ladders, tournaments, clubs, coaches and teams as you type (press / to jump to it; on phones tap the magnifier). See all results opens the Search page, with filters for ruleset, country and region, format, played on and open for registration. Leagues and tournaments can now set an optional region (a country plus a description) in their settings and creation wizards.

title: League money rules
body: League settings has a Money card: the winnings formula (per touchdown, fan attendance, a no-stalling bonus, win and draw bonuses and the BB2025 concession rule, with the rulebook formula one click away), petty cash, the inducement budget rule and an optional treasury cap, per league with an optional override per season or ladder. The defaults keep today's numbers. Changes apply from the next fixture, every change is logged and the other organisers are told, and the league page's house rules panel shows the money rules to coaches.

title: Message boards for leagues and tournaments
body: Leagues and tournaments now have a Board tab for their coaches and organisers. Organisers can pin, lock, hide or delete posts, mute a coach for a while, switch the board off or make it public, and see a Reports queue and a moderation log; coaches can report a post.

title: Ladder redrafts, tournament registration gates and league-time registration dates
body: Ladders now redraft through the same board and Redraft mode as seasons: a team that reaches its set number of ladder games redrafts before its next challenge, and a period end opens a redraft for every team. Tournaments can keep registration shut until a set time with a countdown and Open now; registration opens and closes are typed in the league's time zone; leagues where you only play in a ladder now show in the sidebar.

title: Gates: open a step at a time or with a league night
body: Organisers can keep an online step shut until a set time in the league's time zone, or until a League Event (and it moves with the event): the redraft window, rest rolls and submissions, season start, registration, ladder challenges and the period honours reveal. Coaches see a countdown, and when a gate opens they get a note and the league's Discord gets a post. A new live Redraft rolls page shows every Rest & Relaxation roll, large enough for a screen at the venue.

title: Import your league from a TourPlay export
body: Organisers can upload the export they downloaded from TourPlay (a zip or its CSV files) in League management, TourPlay import, or from the league wizard, preview what comes in and apply it. Matches by NAF name or number and other likely matches are proposed for the organiser to confirm, a re-import keeps results and roster changes made here, and coaches can claim an imported name with "Is this you?" on the league page.

title: Ladder titles: belts, Money in the Bank and the Rumble
body: Ladders can now have a title belt (Ladder settings, Titles). The champion earns bonus points for defences and every week held, the top two contenders play an eliminator for the mandatory title shot, and the champion must defend within 21 days. Money in the Bank contracts, an interim champion, a Rumble knockout and period honours come with it, and the league Overview shows the Current Champions.

title: Clubs: join a club and play for it
body: Create a club or ask to join one in the new Clubs section; its admins approve requests. When you join a league, ladder or tournament you pick which of your clubs you represent, and your results there count for that club on its Members, Results and Stats tabs. Members also get a club board and can choose to hear when a clubmate wins, and admins can connect a Discord webhook for members' results, podiums and league titles.

title: Season and tournament templates you can share
body: Save a season as a template from League management, Templates (or the wizard's Season step), then start a new season from it or from a copy of the last season. Tournament organisers can save a template from Manage or the wizard's Review, start a new tournament from one with check-in times kept relative to the start, and share templates with other organisers, who can use or copy them but not change yours.

title: Tournament registration uses saved teams only
body: The register sheet now offers only your saved teams for the tournament's ruleset, Roster later where the organisers allow it, and Build one now. Super FUMBBL library teams are no longer a team source; a team made in the League Manager is a saved team. Entries already accepted are unchanged, and an old pending entry made with a library team can't be accepted until the coach registers again with a saved team.

title: League ladders: challenge ladders beside your seasons
body: Organisers can start one or more ladders from League management, Ladders: pick rating, points or position swap, league or tournament style, and the challenge rules. Coaches join with a team built for the ladder (straight in when validated) or move a league team in with its progression, then challenge each other from the new Ladder tab; an accepted challenge goes straight to Propose a time. Organisers can also schedule rounds, and the ladder posts results and rank changes to its own Discord webhook.

title: Swap a league team, and teams available for takeover
body: Organisers can swap the team behind a league entry from the team page cog, picking from that coach's saved teams and league teams (teams that don't fit the season are greyed with the reason); a team the coach hasn't shared needs the coach's OK. The entry keeps its standings and fixtures and lists both teams. A team can be marked Available for Takeover on the league overview, where any coach can apply with a saved team or league team, or to take the team over. Coaches can turn on Permit league transfer for a team so it can move to another league with its record. Records follow the coach of each game, so a new coach never inherits past results.

title: League Events: league nights and other events on the calendar
body: Organisers add league nights, drafts, tournament days and socials in League management, Schedule, with weekly or every-few-weeks repeats in the league's time zone. They show on the league Calendar, coaches get a note (and a reminder the day before), the league's Discord gets a "New league event" post, and with the Super FUMBBL bot in your server each event can also be a Discord event.

title: Random skills and characteristic rolls on the team page
body: In season, a player's + menu now offers a Random Primary skill (pick a category, two big D6 roll the table twice, rerolls shown, and you keep one) and Advance Characteristic, where a big D8 rolls and settles before the characteristics it allows appear, with Choose Skill as the alternative. The server rolls, the dice log and the team history record every roll, and a roll waiting for its pick comes back unchanged when you reopen the menu. Organisers can roll on a coach's behalf in Edit mode.

title: League registration: join a league season, organiser approvals and payment references
body: Register a team for a league season from the league page: build it in the Roster Builder under the season's rules (or pick one of your teams when the organisers allow it), choose your region and what the organisers see, then confirm. Organisers accept, waitlist or decline each team in League management, Registrations; accepting adds the team to the season, also mid-season, and each entry gets a payment reference with an "I have paid" button.

title: Fork team routes can require sign-in
body: Team libraries, team creation on the Fork, coach search and records can now be locked to signed-in coaches, and a coach sees only their own team library. The Roster Builder stays open to everyone; saving still needs sign-in.

title: League match teams are removed from Super FUMBBL after the game
body: When a league fixture's Super FUMBBL result is recorded, or Super FUMBBL play is cancelled, the copies of both league teams made for that match are removed from Super FUMBBL automatically. The fixture's history shows when they went.

title: Tournament registration: approvals, waitlist, check-in and payment references
body: Register for a tournament from a three-step sheet: pick a Roster Builder save or register now and add the roster later, choose your region and what the organisers see, then confirm. Organisers can approve each entry from Manage, Registrations, the waitlist moves up on its own when a place opens, coaches check in from the top of the tournament page, and each entry gets a payment reference with an "I have paid" button.

title: Dice roller in the match recorder, and forfeits with defection rolls
body: The recorder has a Dice button: D6, block dice (the opponent picks on -2 and -3, on their own screen), D8, the casualty die and a Kick-off panel for deviate and the kick-off event. Every roll is made on the server and both coaches see it live; a hidden dice log can be shown per match. Organisers can enter a forfeit from the fixtures editor or the recorder, with penalty points, winnings, fans, MVPs and defection rolls for veteran players after an illegal concession.

title: League calendar: week, month and year views
body: The league Calendar tab now has Week, Month and Year views next to the list, remembered for you, with previous, next and Today buttons, all in the league's time zone. Every fixture is a link: unplayed games open the fixture summary, played ones open the match report when the site has one.

title: Team page v2: one team summary, coach editing and organiser edit mode
body: The league team page and the Roster Builder's new Summary step now share one wide team summary with the table-style roster. Coaches edit their own team within the rules (hire, fire and staff before the first game; names, numbers, hires and skills paid with SPP after it), and organisers get an Edit mode for every field, injuries with a band-aid list, Seasons Played, and a status cog to mark a team inactive and decide its unplayed fixtures.

title: Custom stars, ruleset summaries and BB2025 matched play
body: Organisers can create their own Star Players in the Tournament Creator (sprite, stats, cost, skills, plus custom traits and rules that print under "Special rules" in the Roster Builder and on the PDF), share a read-only summary page and PDF of any ruleset, and must now explain a rules change to registered coaches, who are notified and get their rosters re-checked. BB2025 matched play joins the featured rulesets.

title: Fixture summary: the match page before kick-off
body: A league fixture's page now opens with a match summary (team value, record, position, form, petty cash, treasury and inducement budget), coach cards with Rating, win rate and rank, and the coaches' previous meetings with a link to the last one. Coaches pick inducements there in private until both lock, and the picks fill the recorder's picker at the start, where they can still be changed. The coaches' messages are just for the two of you (ask an organiser to bring them in), appear in your Messages inbox, and a new one sends the other coach a note and a Discord message.

title: Weekly Digest marks organiser-typed scores as edited
body: A score an organiser typed or changed shows in the Weekly Digest as "(edited)" and counts as a normal result. Only outcomes an admin decided (forfeits, deadline forfeits, concessions with no recorded game) are labelled as an administrative win, loss or draw, with no score.

title: Weekly Digest now lists every result, and labels administrative ones
body: The Discord Weekly Digest includes hand-entered results as well as recorded games. Forfeits, deadline auto-forfeits, concessions entered by an organiser and organiser overrides of an existing result show as an administrative win, loss or draw (forfeits show no score). Highlights still use recorded games only.

title: League pages: bigger, cleaner text, a two-row header, and tidier overview, fixtures, standings, honours and awards
body: The site now uses one clean sans-serif everywhere at a larger default size, with SNES Italic for the panel headings (Nuffle is retired). League headers show every tab on a second row. The league overview fits on one screen with compact result cards in their own scrolling box; fixture phases collapse (finished ones start collapsed); standings have a phase picker, bigger text, and coach and team names that open a coach summary or the team's roster; Honours has a Player / Coach / Team switch; and Awards shows cards grouped by season or a sortable table, with a pin icon for organisers.

title: Discord for every league, season and tournament
body: Each season and tournament can now post to its own Discord channel (a blank one uses the league's), with a toggle for every event: registrations, pairings, results, standings, champions, awards and news. Games recorded on the tabletop recorder or played on Super FUMBBL post deaths and sent-offs live and finish with an end-of-game digest that includes each coach's comment from the end of the match. Leagues also get a Weekly Digest with standings, results and highlights. Rude words are always shown as *** on Discord, and on the site when you keep Filter profanity on in Account.

title: Browse leagues: bigger cards, a table and search
body: The leagues list is now Browse leagues: large cards with each league’s header art, crest, status, current season, ruleset, teams, dates, region and where it is played, plus a Registration open button when you can join. Switch to a sortable table, filter by status, play mode or open registration, and search by league, team, coach, organiser, region, ruleset or season.

title: Redraft mode in the Roster Builder, and the Redraft board in league management
body: Coaches now redraft in the Roster Builder: roll Rest & Relaxation first, then keep or release each player with their re-hire cost, add hires, staff and rerolls the normal way, and submit against the redraft budget shown on the value bar. Organisers run the Redraft board from League settings -> Redraft, with each team's budget earned against the league's set budget, statuses, a redraft window (no games while it is open) and Lift to budget for one team or all. The budget formula is editable per league, and each team's page shows its current redraft budget.

title: New league and tournament creation steps, with house rules
body: Creating a league or tournament now starts from ruleset cards (BB2025 first, then EuroBowl 2026, Small Gods and World Cup 3.0) and has a House rules group: Prayers to Nuffle, Brawling Brutes, stat increase caps, MVP and hire/fire for leagues, and Progression for tournaments. Tournaments get their own Format step with editable points and a tiebreaker list (points always rank first), plus an option to avoid pairing coaches from the same club or region. Played on (Tabletop or Super FUMBBL) is now a general setting, the Review step has Save as draft and Publish now, and each overview shows a House rules panel. Organisers find Create league and Create tournament in the account menu; other coaches find Ask to organise there.

title: League inducement statistics
body: The league overview's Inducements panel now shows how often each inducement has been taken: times taken and the share of games, for this season or all seasons. It counts games recorded on the site; the season's price list is one click away under Price list.

title: One header for every league, tournament and series page
body: Inside a league, tournament or series every page now shares one slim header: the logo, name and status (a season picker on leagues), the tabs in TourPlay's order (Overview, Fixtures, Standings, Board coming soon, Calendar, Honours, Statistics, Participants, Draws, Awards; tabs with nothing in them yet stay hidden), and your role. Organisers manage from the cog. Team pages, fixture lobbies and tournament games keep the header with a breadcrumb back. Participants is open to everyone with public details only, and organisers can open each coach to see what they shared. Series get Overview, a Schedule of event cards and Standings.

title: PayPal and Venmo links for entry fees
body: Organisers can add a PayPal.Me link and a Venmo username next to the entry fee, in the tournament and league creation steps and later in Manage or League settings. The overview then shows a Pay entry fee block with both buttons. Payment is made directly to the organiser; organisers tick Paid in Participants, and each coach sees only their own payment status.

title: Pages fit a 1920x1080 screen
body: On a desktop screen the page itself no longer scrolls: the top bar, sidebar and page headers stay put and long content scrolls inside its own pane. League and tournament tabs, the Tournament Creator (its Preview columns scroll separately), the Roster Builder's three columns, the coach page, Account, Schedule, Messages, Tabletop, the fixture lobby, the redraft board and the lists all work this way, with table headers that stay in view. On laptops, tablets and phones pages scroll as before.

title: Create your own league
body: Site organisers can now start a league from Create league on the Leagues list: five short steps for the name and artwork, the rules and team building, Season 1 with its registration window, and Discord. A new league stays a draft that only its organisers see until you press Publish in League settings, where Open registration and Start season now live too. Each season keeps its own registration settings (max teams, max per race, approval), copied from the league's defaults.

title: Create a tournament step by step, then publish it
body: Create now opens a page that walks you through the ruleset (or a new one in the Tournament Creator), the details (dates, tabletop venue or Super FUMBBL, format, pairing), and registration (window, places, waitlist, approval, roster deadline, check-in, entry fee, NAF). Save it as a draft only you and your organisers can see, or publish it straight away; Manage has Publish and Unpublish.

title: Build a team for a league
body: The Roster Builder has a league mode: open it from "Build a team for this league" on a league page while registration is open. It uses that season's team-building rules: only the rosters the league allows (official, NAF-approved, unofficial), each race's tier, treasury and starting skills, and the max per race (a full race shows why it can't be picked). The season's inducement table is shown for reference. A saved team keeps the league season, ready for registration.

title: Ask to become an organiser
body: Want to run a league or tournament? Send a short request from your Account page and a site admin will approve or decline it; you get a notification and a Discord message with the answer. Admins review requests in Organiser requests under Testing.

title: A new sign-up: pick your coach name, then your profile
body: Signing in with Discord for the first time now takes two short steps on the site itself: choose your coach name (with a live check, or link a Super FUMBBL account you already have), then check your profile and accept the privacy notice. Your coach page then shows a Get started panel with the next things to do: join a league, enter a tournament, build a team or run your own. Hide it whenever you like.

title: Tournament Creator summary page restyled, and inherited Sevens
body: The Preview tab is now a summary page in the Roster Builder style: Overview, Team building, Skills & advancement, Inducements & stars and Special rules panels with figures, gold prices and on/off chips, and a package summary with the Save button beside it. A package that builds on a Sevens package now shows the Sevens settings on every tab, marked inherited until you change them here.

title: Blood Bowl Sevens in the Roster Builder
body: Build Blood Bowl Sevens teams: pick Sevens Free Create (next to Free Create) or the Blood Bowl Sevens (Matched Play) ruleset. The builder follows the ruleset: 7 to 11 players, a Non-Linemen 3 / 4 counter, Sevens staff prices, the Sevens inducements (incl. Desperate Measures) and Skill Points by tier. Make one Lineman your Veteran (MA −1). Star Players and the fork aren't offered: Sevens is tabletop only. The team sheet and PDF print the Sevens title and mark the Veteran.

title: Blood Bowl Sevens in the Tournament Creator
body: The Tournament Creator has a Format switch: pick Sevens to apply the Blood Bowl Sevens defaults (600k, 7 to 11 players, at most 4 non-Linemen, one Veteran, Sevens staff prices and inducements, no stars), then change any of them. There is also a ready-made Blood Bowl Sevens (Matched Play) package with the Sevens tier list. Sevens is tabletop only.

title: Fixture lobbies for tournament matches
body: Each tournament match now has a lobby where the two coaches chat, lock their submitted rosters, pick inducements under the tournament's rules and start the game. Inducements bought in the Roster Builder show up already filled in and can't be removed. Open it with Lobby on your tournament's My entry or Rounds, from the sidebar, or from an agreed game on the Schedule.

title: Organisers can edit inducements after the start
body: The match recorder's Admin panel has Edit inducements: the same picker for either team, priced by the match's league or tournament table. Each change is logged as an admin event, can be undone like one, and the treasury is charged by the latest picks when the result is confirmed.

title: Choose a new Team Captain for tabletop teams
body: When a tabletop team's captain dies, its team picker shows Captain vacant: choose, and the coach or an organiser picks a new captain who gains Team Captain and Pro for free. The choice is saved as its own team revision, so undoing a later match keeps it.

title: Jaguar Warrior name
body: Amazon's Jaguar Warrior Blocker now shows as just Jaguar Warrior in the Roster Builder, the Sheet and PDF, and the team pages. The full name stays as the tooltip.

title: Players by position in the Roster summary
body: Under Players, the Roster summary now lists how many of each position you have, such as 2× Jaguar Warrior, in the hire list's order with star players after. It updates as you hire and fire.

title: Finer stat increase rules for organisers
body: The Tournament Creator's Advanced tab has a Stat increases section: pick positions or keywords (such as Big Guy or Lineman) that can't advance, block a stat for everyone or for chosen players, and cap increases per team. The Advance dialog greys out each blocked button and says which tournament rule applies, and the validator enforces the same rules.

title: Reset a player, and stat increases follow the ruleset
body: The Advance dialog has a RESET switch that takes a player back to base: every added skill and stat increase goes, while the name, number and Team Captain stay. Rulesets that don't allow stat increases now show the stat bar greyed out with the reason, and the Tournament Creator has an Allow stat increases switch (Advanced) that the validator enforces.

title: Discord messages for game-time proposals
body: When a coach proposes, changes or accepts a game time with you, the Super FUMBBL bot now also messages you on Discord with a link to answer it. It's on for everyone with Discord linked; turn it off on your Account page under Notifications. You need to share a Discord server with the bot.

title: Player names in the Roster Builder
body: Every player you hire now gets a name that fits the race. Click a name (or press Enter or F2 on it) to rename the player, or use the reroll button for another one. Names are kept in saves, share links, teams created on the fork and the PDF sheet, which now shows each player's name over their position and your team's name as its title.

title: One + button for skills and stat increases
body: Roster Builder rows now have a single + button. It opens an Advance dialog with the skill list and, where the ruleset allows stat increases (such as Free Create), the player's stat bar with + and − buttons for each characteristic. Elite skills now show a small diamond.

title: Propose a time for your fixtures
body: Agree when to play a league fixture or tournament match with your opponent: offer up to three 2-hour times, and they accept one, suggest others or decline. The agreed time is saved on the fixture and shows on your new Schedule page (month, week, day and list views), with warnings for late hours in your opponent's timezone.

title: Organisers can correct tournament results
body: Tournament organisers can now edit or clear a confirmed result from Manage, Rounds. Standings, statistics, series points and the podium update at once, both coaches are told, and the fixture shows an Edited chip with who changed it.

title: Fixture lobbies with pre-match inducements
body: Every pending league fixture now has a lobby where the two coaches chat, lock their rosters, buy inducements against the team value gap (with Auto-Buy for the underdog) and press Ready, then start the match. Open it from Lobby on the Fixtures tab or your next fixture in the sidebar.

title: Choose a new Team Captain
body: If your Team Captain is killed, fired, retired or not re-hired at a redraft, your team sheet now shows a Captain vacant chip and asks you to choose a new captain the next time you open it. Pick any roster player who is not a Big Guy or a Star: they gain Team Captain and Pro for free, and the old captain keeps theirs in the team's history.

title: Tournament statistics, honours and awards
body: Every tournament page has three new tabs. Statistics shows records by team and by coach (touchdowns, casualties, completions, interceptions, fouls, injuries and deaths, best defence) and race win rates, with only the stats its results record. Honours shows the top five for each stat for teams, players and coaches. Awards shows the podium once the tournament finishes, and organisers can give their own awards, which also appear on the coach's page.

title: League inducements, including your own
body: League organisers and admins have a new Inducements tab in league settings: turn each standard inducement on or off, set its cap and price per season, and add the league's own inducement types with an icon, a category and a short effect. Coaches see the season's table on the league page.

title: League fixture deadlines
body: League organisers can now set a deadline for each round, and give any fixture its own. Every unplayed fixture shows its deadline (amber under 72 hours, red under 24 hours, then Overdue), and so do your next fixture in the sidebar and the Deadlines panel on your coach page. Organisers can also turn on auto-forfeit for a season (off by default): once a deadline passes, the fixture is marked for an organiser to decide, recorded as no result, or lost by both teams, and both coaches and the organisers are told.

title: Friends, private messages and blocking
body: Your coach page now has a Friends list (send, accept or decline friend requests, plus People you know: coaches you have played) and a Messages preview. The new Messages page holds private one-to-one conversations with other coaches, on the site only, with unread counts on Home. You can block a coach from their row or a conversation: they can't message you or send you friend requests, and you can unblock them under Messages.

title: Tournament Series
body: Organisers and admins can now group tournaments into a series with its own page: the tournaments with dates and status, and combined standings across them (every event counts, or each coach's best N). A series also sets the starting pairing (Dutch, Monrad or Elo seeded) for new tournaments created in it, and the tournament page's Series chip links to the series.

title: League awards and a Hall of Fame
body: League organisers and admins can now give awards from the league Honours tab: a title, an icon, a team or coach of the league (for one season or league-wide) and a note. The coach is notified, and the award shows on their coach page and on the team's page. The Honours tab also has a Hall of Fame with one card per finished season (champion, runner-up and dates) and entries organisers pin: a season champion, an award or a record.

title: League Participants tab for organisers
body: League organisers and admins now have a Participants tab on each season: every team with Paid, Verified, Frozen, Checked in and Active (or standby) switches, plus Mark all paid, Mark all verified, Check in all and clearing in one go, for all teams or the ones you tick. Coaches get a notification when their flags change, and the table shows only the contact details a coach chose to share with the league.

title: League standings update live and seasons crown a champion
body: The league Standings tab now builds its tables from the results as they come in (fixtures editor and Super FUMBBL results): points (win 3, draw 1, loss 0), games, wins, draws, losses, touchdowns, casualties, the stats the results recorded, the last six results as coloured dots, and your own team highlighted. Ties go to touchdown difference, casualty difference, then head-to-head. Finish season now proposes a podium (Champion, Runner-up, Consolation) from the playoff final or the final standings; organisers can change it before confirming, and the champion shows on the league Overview, Honours and the statistics page. A season finished here can be reopened, which clears its podium.

title: Your leagues in the sidebar
body: The Leagues section of the sidebar now lists each league you play in this season, with your team, its win-draw-loss record and your next fixture, which opens its summary. Two dead links are gone: the Series chip on a tournament is plain text until series pages exist, and league registration settings now point to the Teams tab.

title: League announcements and fixtures table view
body: Organisers now post league news and message members from one Announcement button on the league header, and the dialog always posts to the season it was opened on. The Fixtures tab gains a round bar with Previous and Next, phase and team filters that reset per season, and a Cards or Table switch that the site remembers for you.

title: Site-wide restyle
body: The sign-in card, Account page, Standings, the tournament page and its Manage views, team pages, league settings, organiser tools and their dialogs, the match recorder setup and the smaller pages now share the same panels, tabs, buttons and tables as the Roster Builder and league page. Buttons that delete something use a strong scarlet fill so their labels stay readable.

title: NAF from your profile
body: When you register for a NAF-sanctioned tournament, the NAF name and number on your profile fill in automatically and go to the organisers, and you are told. If you have none you can add it to your profile on the spot, or declare that you are not a NAF member.

title: Organiser sharing and NAF-sanctioned registration
body: You now choose, per league and per tournament, which contact details its organisers may see; nothing is shared by default, and the Account page has a Sharing panel to change it. Organisers are told about every new registration, tournaments can be marked NAF-sanctioned, and your contact details take a country and at most one phone number.

title: Download and delete your data
body: The Account page has a Privacy panel: download everything the site holds about you as a ZIP file, or ask for your account to be deleted. Deleting keeps past results but shows them as a deleted coach instead of your name; deletion opens when the site goes live.

title: Portal mail
body: League organisers can message their members through the site without ever seeing an email address, and you control league email from the Email panel on the Account page. Every message honours your consent and unsubscribe choice at the moment it is sent; delivery starts when the site goes live.

title: Onboarding
body: After your first sign-in a Welcome dialog asks you to accept the privacy notice and set your preferred name and contact details; until then the site is read-only for you. Organisers see only what you choose to share, Discord ids are never shown to other coaches, and NAF details are edited only by tournament organisers for their own entrants.

title: Privacy notice
body: A public Privacy page explains what the site stores, why, how long it keeps it and how to reach us. It describes only features that are live today.

title: Match log order
body: The match log now reads from top to bottom, and the live feed follows the latest entry.

title: League header
body: The league page header shows the league name in the title font with its seasons badge and a Founded tag, and gains a Statistics tab. The season row now runs oldest to newest, and the chosen season stays selected as you move between tabs.

title: Light theme
body: The light theme is now derived from the dark one as soft greys, so both themes match. Switch with the sun and moon button at the foot of the sidebar.

title: Coach avatars
body: Upload your own coach avatar from the Account page; your Discord picture is the fallback. Result cards show the avatars of both coaches.

title: Free Create in the Roster Builder
body: A Free Create card replaces the BB2025 default ruleset, with an Ignore in-game limits option for building any team you like. Characteristic caps, the 8-skill limit and 16 players still apply, and shared Free Create teams show their builder prices.

title: Roster Builder redesign
body: The Tournament Builder is now the Roster Builder, with its Ruleset, Roster and Sheet steps in the page header. The Ruleset step shows rulesets and Pick a race side by side, the roster shows players as cards with a Team Captain badge and + Skill buttons, hire cards show cost and count at a glance, and accordion panels open in place.

title: New result cards
body: Past games show as result cards with both teams' colours, a big race crest with the race underneath, the competition under the score and room for coach avatars. The cards stack to fit the width of the page.

title: Welcome page for visitors
body: Visitors who are not signed in now see a League Manager welcome page with a short introduction, a sign-in button and recent games.

title: Sidebar and header refresh
body: The header has a Discord Login button and shows the page title next to the wordmark, gold on Tournaments and Leagues pages. The sidebar gains Browse Leagues, Build a team and Browse Tournaments buttons, a sun and moon theme switch, and a collapse tab at its bottom edge.

title: Sheet step previews the PDF
body: The Roster Builder's Sheet step now shows the exported team sheet on paper, exactly as the PDF prints it. The PDF gains a tournament ruleset box at the top right of the first page.

title: Page titles in the header
body: Each page's title now sits in the header bar instead of repeating at the top of the page, and the sidebar category names use the wordmark lettering.

title: Turn-by-turn log for online games
body: Game pages for games played on Super FUMBBL now show a turn-ordered match log, read once from each finished game's replay.

title: Roster Builder moves into the site
body: The team builder for tournaments now runs inside the site, with skills, stars and inducements on one pane and the roster, team controls and validator together on the Roster step. Old builder links take you to the new page.

title: Tournament Creator moves into the site
body: Organisers now edit tournament rulesets in the site's Tournament Creator, with tabs for the overview, tiers, team rules, skills, stars, inducements, advanced settings and a preview.

title: Create Tournament dialog
body: Organisers can start a new tournament from the Create Tournament button on the Tournaments page or from the account menu.

title: Game pages open the match report
body: A finished game's page now opens the match report in a read-only view with the full squads, fouls, winnings and league result details.

title: League team values recomputed
body: League team values are now worked out by the league from each player's stored value plus staff after every change, and the current team value leaves out players who miss the next game.

title: More detail from league games on Super FUMBBL
body: Results of league games played on Super FUMBBL now record whether a concession was legal, casualties suffered, attendance and extra player counters, and show them on the fixture summary, the game page and the roster. Slann teams and the Ball & Chain now build correctly for those games.

title: League statistics cards; rosters always visible; assign a coach to a team
body: The league statistics page now opens each rules edition (BB2020, BB2025, All time) with a row of spotlight cards: top scorer, casualty leader, most valuable player, best coach record, best team, biggest win, playmaker, interceptor, dirtiest player and iron man. Each card shows the big number, who holds it, their team and race with the race crest, the seasons it came from and anyone tied with them, and opens the player, the team or the match. On a phone the cards scroll sideways. The leader tables are still below. Team rosters are now always visible to everyone: the Hide team composition setting is gone. Redraft rookies never receive Team building starting skills, only the skills printed for their position. Organisers can assign a Super FUMBBL coach account to a league team from its roster on the Teams tab (for this season or every season of the team); the account is seated on the team’s fixtures that have no result yet, so a test league game can be played with it, and the change is logged on the season.

title: Result banking uses stored player values; no pre-game guard
body: A death, a missed game or a team-value adjustment now uses the player's stored value, which the fork team file carries from the league roster, and only prices skills when that value is absent. The fallback pricing is Primary skill 20,000, Secondary 40,000, Elite skill = the player's access price for its category + 10,000, with traits free and unknown skills still quarantining the result. The check that refused teams the banker could not price before a game is removed.

title: Leagues: overlapping seasons, news, Discord events, tier shortcut
body: A new season can now start while another is still in progress: the newest season becomes the current one, and Finish season lets organisers pick which open season to close. The Redraft board picks which finished season to redraft from and which season receives the draft lists (by default the newest finished season into the newest season in progress). League news is here: organisers post news on the league Overview (pin, edit, delete; simple formatting), the season’s coaches are notified, and the post goes to the league Discord. Organisers also get a fixtures editor on the Fixtures tab: add a fixture (home, away, round, date, or a test fixture), change its date, enter or clear the result, and delete one that has no result. Every Discord toggle is now wired: league news, fixture created, match started and match result post through the league webhook when switched on, with a [Test] tag on test fixtures. On the Team building tab, each roster row has Apply to all rosters in this tier, which copies its starting treasury and Primary, Secondary and Elite starting skills to every roster of the same tier (it asks first before overwriting values already set); save to keep them.

title: League fixtures can be played on Super FUMBBL
body: When a league plays on Super FUMBBL and an organiser allows a fixture, its summary page (Summary on any fixture in the Fixtures tab) now has Generate fixture on Super FUMBBL. Either coach or an organiser can press it: both league teams are built on Super FUMBBL from their league rosters (players, skills, injuries, SPP, staff and treasury as the league has them), the game is scheduled, the opponent is told "<Coach> has invited you to play your match on Super FUMBBL", and the organisers hear about it too. Pressing it again re-uses the same teams and game. Each coach then gets Start Game on Super FUMBBL, which downloads their own launch file; nobody else can take it. The page shows where things stand: teams built, game scheduled, in progress, result recorded, or failed with the reason, and organisers can reset a failed game (with a reason that goes in the history), allow a late launch, or cancel Super FUMBBL play for that fixture. When the game ends the result comes back by itself: the score, casualties and player lines go on the fixture, and both league teams are updated from the game the same way Super FUMBBL updates its own teams (SPP, injuries, deaths, missed games, winnings into the treasury, dedicated fans). Both coaches get a notification and the result posts to the league's Discord channel when that is switched on.

title: League redraft: board for organisers, re-hire flow for coaches
body: Start redraft in League settings now opens the Redraft board. Organisers see every team of the finished season, plus an Inactive tab for teams from earlier seasons that sat it out, with games played, wins, draws and losses, treasury and the redraft budget: the starting treasury, plus the treasury left, 20k per league game, 20k per win and 10k per draw, capped at 1,300k unless the league turns the cap off. Tick the teams to redraft (or Check all), override a budget with a reason, and Confirm redraft: each coach is told, and the league Discord hears about it. Coaches open their redraft from the notification or from their team page. First comes Rest and Relaxation: each niggling injury rolls off on a 4+, or a 3+ with an Apothecary, rolled by the site or entered from the tabletop; missed games clear. Then the Team Draft List: re-hire players at their value plus a 20k agent fee for every season they have played (players not re-hired retire), keep or drop rerolls, assistant coaches, cheerleaders and the Apothecary, hire new players from the roster, and watch the remaining budget as you go. The submitted list becomes the team for the next season, straight away if it has started or as soon as it does, and the organisers can follow progress on the board and close the redraft when it is done.

title: Match recorder: random seats, away team calls, Discord result summary, spectator view
body: Home and away are now drawn at random when a match is created (casual, tournament and test matches alike), and the draw is in the match log; an organiser can swap them before the first pre-game roll, which is logged too. The away team calls the coin toss, so there is no separate caller draw any more. When a match is confirmed, the final result (score, touchdown scorers, casualties, MVPs and any concession, with a link to the game page) is posted to Discord through the recorder webhook, marked [Test] for test matches. Anyone can now watch a match read-only at its recorder link: signed-in coaches who are not playing, and visitors for any match that is not a test match. Watchers see the scoreboard, the pre-game steps and cines as they happen and the match log, with no buttons, and the kick or receive choice shows as waiting for the coach who won the toss.

title: League settings: administration, information, registrations, team building, connections
body: League organisers and site admins now have a cog at the right end of the league header strip that opens League settings, in five tabs. Administration lists who runs the league (the owner, the organisers, who the owner adds or removes by coach name, and the site admins), starts a new season (numbered automatically, with its ruleset, carrying over the team building rules) and finishes the open season; Start redraft shows where the redraft board will go. Information holds the name, full name, description, default ruleset and where the league plays, with addresses checked for the United States (state and ZIP code) and Canada (province and postal code). Registrations sets which rosters may sign up, whether sign-up is open, hiding team composition and the limits per league and per race. Team building is a table of every roster with its tier, starting treasury and the extra starting skills the league grants (primary, secondary, elite), saved per season for the Tournament Team Builder to use. External connections downloads the results as spreadsheets (teams, fixtures, standings, participants, honours, awards), connects a Discord channel (the webhook address is kept private and only ever shown masked; a test post checks it) and turns on Play on Super FUMBBL, after which league admins can allow single fixtures, and both coaches and the organisers are told. The league name on the league page is now white and the logo sits centred in its strip.

title: Match recorder: pre-game fans, weather, inducements and coin flip
body: Every recorded match, test matches included, now walks the pre-game before Turn 1: the fans (D3 plus dedicated fans, with a short crowd cine), the weather (2D6 cine and a splash with what the weather does), journeymen, an inducement picker with prices, limits, petty cash and treasury, prayers to Nuffle, then the coin flip: the site draws which coach calls, everyone watches the coin land, and the winner picks Kick or Receive. Every roll can be made by the site (Roll for me) or typed in from the table (Enter result), and every step lands in the match log. Organisers can skip the pre-game (logged). Each milestone can also be posted to Discord for the BloodBowl bot when the recorder webhook is configured.

title: League players get stable ids
body: Every player in an imported league now has their own id, so two players who share a name are never mixed up. The id stays the same every time the league is re-imported, and the same player is linked across seasons (same team, shirt number, name and position), so career totals follow the player, not the name. Statistics leaders, the Honours boards and the roster rows all work from these ids, and a name in the leaders or an honours board opens that player's team with their row marked. When the TourPlay export lists two players of one team under the same name and position it still cannot say which of them earned the totals, so that total is shown once on the team and, in muted text, as a shared total on both players' rows.

title: Game pages: open any result for its summary and match report
body: Every card in Past Games now opens a page for that game. The result card sits at the top, followed by a summary: when it was played, the competition and round, casualties caused and suffered, any concession and the MVPs, plus each team’s scorers, casualty-makers and a player table when the game was played through the site (otherwise the page says per-player stats are recorded for games played through the site). Tabletop matches also show the match report: the key moments by half and turn, both teams’ finished-game summaries, and an Open match reporter button. Tournament fixtures link to the tournament’s Rounds tab.

title: Team sheet header: avatar click to upload, cleaner title row
body: The team sheet header is re-laid out: the avatar box on the left spans both rows, the team name takes the full width of the first row, and the second row has the race and special rules on the left with the coach name on the right (hover it for the last-updated date). The Team and On the fork status block and the Coach label are gone, on the share page too. On your own team page the avatar is now a button: hover or focus it and an Upload plate appears; click it to open the Team avatar dialog. On phones the avatar shrinks to 72 px and the name, rules and coach stack beneath it.

title: Leagues: TABBL with six seasons and all-time statistics
body: Leagues now have their own pages. TABBL, the Tahoma Area Blood Bowl League, is on the site with all six seasons: every fixture and score, the standings for each phase and division, each team's end-of-season roster with skills, SPP and the season's touchdowns, casualties and MVPs, the honour boards and the awards. The league page shows the Season 6 header bar with the TABBL logo, a Season picker (newest first, each marked BB2020 or BB2025), and tabs for Overview, Standings, Fixtures, Teams and Honours. The latest results show as wide result cards in the two teams' colours. A Statistics page adds career leaders, coach and team records, race win rates, biggest wins and champions, with a BB2020 / BB2025 / All time switch on top. League organisers can upload a logo and a header bar.

title: Mini calendar on the coach page
body: The Account box on the coach page is gone. In its place a Mini calendar shows the current month (Monday first, today outlined in green), a dot on every day with a deadline or fixture in that deadline's colour, previous and next month buttons, and an Upcoming list of your next five events from today onward, across months, each linking to its tournament or fixture. Full calendar opens the whole thing on the Account page. My teams now sits below it. Each team tile shows the competition it is registered in (or Not registered) and its current team value, and carries a red badge with the number of things still to do: advancement rolls waiting to be finished, players with an advancement they can afford, and roster problems flagged on a registration.

title: Sprite icons on the content panels
body: Every content box now carries a small pixel sprite before its title, in the same hand-drawn style as the sidebar: a newspaper for What's new, a hand bell for Notifications, an hourglass for Deadlines, a football for Recent games, two figures for Friends, a sealed envelope for Messages, a banner for My teams and a shield for Account. The Account page gets a nameplate (Identity), a calendar leaf, a chain link (Connections) and a clock (Set schedule); My teams, Leaderboards, Help, the tournament list and the tournament panels get theirs too. All original art, drawn for both the dark and the light theme.

title: Team avatar upload moved to the team page
body: The Avatars panel on My teams is gone. Open a team from My teams and use the new Team avatar button next to Share: it opens a dialog with the current avatar (or the race crest), a file picker, Upload and Remove. Pictures are cropped square and shrunk to fit, PNG, JPEG or WebP up to 512 KB. After you upload or remove, the team banner updates straight away and the dialog stays open. Teams that already have an avatar still show it on their My teams tile.

title: Team sheet totals: centred, bevelled, scoreboard numerals
body: The totals bar on the shared team sheet and the team management page now has centred, bevelled cells that sit lifted on a drop edge, with the values in the pixel heading font and the scoreboard's dark text shadow (TOTAL larger, keeping its tint). On the management page the Advancement column is now as narrow as its buttons (the header text is hidden but still read by screen readers), and the Add Skill / Add Stat buttons are bevelled and lifted: they rise on hover and press down on click.

title: Sidebar carets on the right; conceded games marked on result cards
body: Sidebar: the collapse caret now sits at the right end of each category header. Leaderboards and Help are plain links with no sub-list, and Testing Tools is now just Testing. Games: Recent games is now Past Games, a scrollable box of larger cards (two across on a wide screen) showing as many games as the server returns. A conceded game now says "Conceded by <coach>" and puts a red-framed plate behind its score; the struck-through team name is gone. Game cards are now bevelled panels that lift when you point at them. Team names such as <script>brains? no longer show as <script>: online-game results were stored with the fork's XML escaping and then escaped again by the page.

title: Connections: link and verify your NAF record
body: The Discord line on the Account page is now a Connections table: Discord, NAF and FUMBBL, each with a Linked / Not linked / Verified chip. Discord stays read-only: it is how you sign in. For the NAF, Link NAF account asks for your NAF coach name and number and checks them against your public NAF coach page; when both match the row turns Verified. The NAF has no sign-in or OAuth for other sites, so Verified means the record exists and matches what you entered, not proof that it is yours, and NAF sign-in is not possible. Re-verify checks again, Unlink removes the name and number, and editing either on your profile clears the check. Your FUMBBL name links through the FUMBBL name field, or shows as locked when tournament registration set it.

title: Recent games on the landing page
body: The page you see before signing in now shows the latest games played through the site, under the sign-in card, and the same strip closes the main column of your coach page. Each card shows both teams with their crests, races and coaches either side of the score, casualties in brackets under each number when they are known, and a tint of the two teams' colours. Tournament games say which tournament and round they belong to, tabletop games say Tabletop, and online games say Online. A tournament or tabletop card opens its page.

title: Sidebar polish: sprite icons, Resources, collapser in the top bar
body: The sidebar icons are redrawn as little retro game sprites: a house, a pennant, a trophy, a podium with a star, a question scroll, a treasure chest, a hammer, a rulebook, a television, a mountain shield and a globe, in greens, golds, browns and blues instead of all red. They are a little bigger too, and bigger again on the narrow rail. Useful resources is now just Resources. The button that folds the sidebar to the rail has moved up into the top bar, at the right edge of the sidebar; the [ key still does the same.

title: Set schedule from the calendar
body: The weekly availability editor is no longer a panel of its own on the Account page. The Calendar now has a Set schedule button beside Deadlines; it opens the editor in a dialog with your timezone, the seven day columns and Save availability. Saving reshades the calendar straight away. Close, Escape and a click outside close the dialog (a click outside is ignored while you have unsaved changes, and your edits are kept if you close and reopen). Links to /account#schedule open the dialog. On a phone the dialog fills the screen minus a small margin and scrolls inside.

title: New sidebar: Home, Leagues, Tournaments, Leaderboards, Help, resources
body: The left sidebar has a new layout. Home sits on top and still carries your unread badge. Below it come Leagues, Tournaments, Leaderboards and Help, each with its own pixel icon, and a Useful resources list linking Blood Bowl Base, Blood Bowl Dave, TABBL and FUMBBL in a new tab. Your own tournaments, teams and fixtures now sit under Tournaments. Every category folds open and shut with its arrow, and the sidebar remembers how you left it; Useful resources starts folded. On the narrow rail you see just the icons: click one to open the sidebar at that section. Leaderboards and Help are new pages: rankings arrive with league play. Account has moved to the menu under your name in the top bar.

title: Account page: identity, schedule and calendar
body: The Account page is rebuilt in the coach page style. Identity lets you set the display name other coaches see (it defaults to your coach name), your FUMBBL name and your NAF name and number; your avatar and the Discord account you sign in with are shown read-only. A FUMBBL name linked through tournament registration stays locked. Schedule is the weekly availability editor, unchanged. Calendar shows a month at a time, Monday first, with your registration and check-in deadlines, report-by deadlines and fixture deadlines as chips coloured like the Deadlines panel; each chip opens its tournament or match, and your usual availability is shaded on the matching days. On a phone the month becomes an agenda list. Proposed match times will appear here once that feature lands.

title: Player sheet on the team management page
body: Click a player on your team management page (the name in the table, or the top of the card on phones) and their player sheet pops out: number, position and sprite, the five characteristics with increases marked, printed, added and free Team Captain skills, SPP against the next advancement with a progress bar and the rank name under it, and the career stats the team file records: touchdowns, casualties caused, completions, interceptions, MVPs, fouls and niggling injuries, plus injuries and value with its breakdown (position cost + added). Stats are recorded for games played through the site; anything not recorded shows a dash, and games played are not tracked yet. Add Skill and Add Stat work from the sheet just like the row buttons. Escape closes it and focus goes back to the player.

title: Tournaments list in the site's design
body: The Tournaments page now looks like the rest of the site. The Active / Upcoming / Finished pills, which could stretch into tall capsules with a big empty gap above them, are replaced by a compact square switch next to the search box, right under the page title. It works with the keyboard too: arrow keys move between the three choices. Each tournament is a panel card with its banner (or the ruleset crest when there is none), a status chip, the dates (or Not set), ruleset, format, entrants and places left, and the round. The button at the bottom fits you: Manage for organisers, Your entry when you are registered, Register while places are open, otherwise Open. On a phone the cards stack in one column.

title: Simpler sidebar: Home carries the unread badge
body: The Coach page section is gone from the left sidebar: it was one page with a long list of links to itself. Home, in the Pages list, now carries a small badge instead. It shows your unread notifications (and, once they arrive, unread messages and proposed match times), updates as they come in, and disappears when there is nothing waiting. On the narrow rail the Home letter keeps a little count in its corner. The bell's list and the sections on the Home page are unchanged.

title: Tournament pages: banner, details and news
body: A tournament now has a front page of its own. Organisers can upload a banner (landscape, up to 1 MB), set the location, start time, entry fee, a summary and notes, registration and check-in deadlines, and post news; pinned posts stay on top. Text supports bold, italic, links and lists. Entrants get a notification when news is posted. The ruleset links open the Tournament Team Builder with the package preselected, and Edit ruleset opens the Tournament Creator.

title: Notifications from the bell
body: Tap the bell in the top bar and your latest notifications pop out right under it: the eight most recent, newest first, each with its icon, title, a one-line preview, how long ago it came and a dot while it is unread. Choosing one marks it read and takes you to it. Mark all read and a link to all your notifications sit at the bottom, and when there is nothing yet it says Nothing to read! Escape, tapping elsewhere or changing page closes it, and it works with the keyboard and on phones.

title: Team management page
body: Your team tiles on the coach page and on My teams now open a team management page laid out like the shared team view. For teams on the fork, each player shows SPP, rank and advancements, with Add Skill when they can afford a random or chosen Primary skill and Add Characteristic when they can afford the characteristic roll; random rolls are saved on the team until you pick. Tournament Builder sheets show read-only until the team plays on the fork. Share, Open in Tournament Builder and Back to My teams sit at the top. My teams now uses the coach page look, with avatars and build links in the side column.

title: Team Captain nomination in the team builders
body: Human, Orc and every other roster with the Team Captain special rule can now nominate a Team Captain in both the Team Builder and the Tournament Builder. Tap the round C beside a player to nominate them; picking another player moves the captaincy, and tapping it again clears it. Big Guys and Star Players cannot be captain, and the C never shows for rosters without the rule. The captain gains Pro for free: it adds nothing to skill cost or team value and never counts towards a tournament's skill limits. The nomination is optional, so the team summary shows "not nominated" as a hint rather than a problem. It is kept when you save, reload or share a team, prints on the roster sheet with a C marker and Pro, and the built team gives the game server both Team Captain and Pro. In a match, a team reroll used while the captain is on the pitch can come back free on a 6.

title: Coach page: What's new on top, availability editor fix
body: What's new now sits at the top of the coach page above Notifications. Editing a time in the weekly availability grid no longer re-sorts the column under your cursor; the blocks stay where they are until you save.

title: Notifications for coaches
body: Your coach page now has a Notifications panel, and the bell in the top bar shows how many you have not read. You get a notification when an organiser marks you paid, verifies or freezes your roster, checks you in or moves you to standby; when the roster check finds problems with your team; when a round is drawn and you have a fixture; and when a result you played is confirmed. Organisers hear when a coach withdraws. Organisers can also send you a message from the Participants table (Message coach), and it shows up here. Tap a notification to open the tournament, or use Mark all read.

title: Drag to reorder players in the Team Builder and Tournament Builder
body: Every roster row now has a gripper on the left. Drag a row with the mouse or a finger to reorder your players, or focus the gripper and press Alt+Up / Alt+Down. Player numbers follow the new order, and the printed sheet and PDF keep it too.

title: Easier-to-read recorder on the light theme and phones
body: Coach names use a darker green on the light theme so they read against the pale hero. On phones the Admin row stays folded behind the Admin chip until you tap it, giving the feed its height back.

title: NAF record line on the scoreboard
body: The match recorder's scoreboard shows each coach's NAF Glicko rating and W/T/L record, read from the coach's NAF page and refreshed when a fixture starts.

title: Coach titles by percentile
body: Coach titles now come from the coach's percentile in the active pool: Legend is the top 2 %, and a coach with fewer than 10 games is a Rookie.

title: Phone layout for the match recorder
body: The match recorder fits a 375 px phone: actions open in bottom sheets and every tap target is bigger.

title: Tournaments: submissions, roster lock, pairing, roles
body: Coaches submit a team and see whether it is valid; the opponent's team can be viewed; organisers lock rosters and start the event in one click, pair rounds with Dutch or Monrad, and run it from the Manage tab. Admins get a tournaments page.

title: Coach page and the new site navigation
body: A left navigation bar with League, Tournament and Coach page trees: your tournaments with their status, your registered team and whether it is valid, and your next fixture. It folds to a narrow icon rail (press [) and becomes a drawer on phones. The new Coach page gathers your deadlines (green, amber under 72 hours, scarlet under 24 hours, grey when overdue, shown in your timezone), your weekly availability on a 7-day grid, your teams, and this What's new list. Notifications, friends and messages arrive in the next lanes.
